title: U.S. House · Utah's 4th District
area: Central Utah under the congressional map first used in 2026, drawn by a Third District Court after the Legislature's 2021 map was struck down; largely overlaps the old 3rd District, including Provo and Utah County.

context.text: Utah's congressional map was redrawn for 2026 by court order in League of Women Voters v. Utah State Legislature. Incumbent Mike Kennedy — who previously represented the old 3rd District — advanced from the Republican primary for this newly drawn 4th District without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled. Rep. Burgess Owens (R), the outgoing incumbent of the old 4th District, filed to run in this district but did not make the primary ballot; he is not seeking re-election.

candidates.name: Mike Kennedy
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled

summary.text: Mike Kennedy is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election, running in the newly drawn 4th District after representing the old 3rd District since January 2025. A family physician and attorney who served in the Utah House and Senate, he sits on the Natural Resources, Transportation and Infrastructure, and Science, Space, and Technology committees. His House website says he is focused on fiscal responsibility, border security and pushing back against federal overreach.

background.text: Born in Lansing, Michigan; his House website says he was raised by a single mother alongside six siblings and held his first job at age 12.
Served a two-year mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, then earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University.
Earned an M.D. from Michigan State University in 1998 and became a family physician.

Earned a J.D. from Brigham Young University's J. Reuben Clark Law School in 2007; his House website says he pursued the degree to better advocate for his patients. Career experience includes work as a family doctor, attorney and small business owner.
Elected to the Utah House of Representatives, District 27, serving 2013 to 2019.
Ran for the Republican nomination for U.S. Senate in 2018 and lost the June 26, 2018 primary to Mitt Romney, 71.3% to 28.7%.
Served in the Utah State Senate from 2021 to 2025, representing District 14 and then District 21; he chaired the Senate Health and Human Services Committee during 2021-2024.

Elected to the U.S. House from Utah's 3rd District in 2024, winning the June 25, 2024 Republican primary with 38.8% in a five-candidate field and the general election with 66.4%; sworn in January 2025.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) serves on the Committee on Natural Resources (vice chair of the Federal Lands subcommittee; Indian and Insular Affairs), the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
His House website says he has been married to his wife, Katrina, for 35 years and that they have raised eight children and have 12 grandchildren.

priorities.text: Says Washington has "a spending problem" and supports meaningful caps on discretionary spending and rooting out waste and duplication across federal agencies.
priorities.quote: Utah families don't get to spend money they don't have and neither should Washington.

priorities.text: Supports an "all-of-the-above" energy approach, including oil, natural gas, nuclear and geothermal production, and says he wants to cut federal permitting red tape so states can lead on energy development.
priorities.quote: I support an all-of-the-above energy approach that embraces American oil, natural gas, nuclear, geothermal, and all other energy production.

positions.summary: Supports expanding oil, natural gas and other fossil-fuel production and cutting federal permitting regulations, rather than accelerating a transition away from fossil fuels.
Describes himself as a fiscal conservative focused on spending cuts and caps on discretionary spending rather than raising revenue through taxes.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Vice Chair, Federal Lands subcommittee), the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, and the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Kennedy has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; positions here are drawn from his official House website issue pages. Federal key floor votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately by script.

candidates.name: Jonny Larsen
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after the primary was canceled

summary.text: Jonny Larsen is the Democratic nominee for Utah's 4th Congressional District. A Marine Corps combat veteran who grew up in Salt Lake City, he worked as a systems and network administrator and describes himself as a VA patient and cancer survivor. His campaign emphasizes the cost of living, Medicare and Social Security, veterans' health care and banning stock trading by elected officials.

background.text: Grew up in a Salt Lake City trailer park; says his mother placed him in a group home at age thirteen and that his grandmother then took him in.
Says he began working at twelve delivering newspapers for the Deseret News and was a night supervisor at Cinnabon by sixteen.
Earned a high school diploma from West High School.

Enlisted in the U.S. Marine Corps at seventeen and served from 2000 to 2004; says he deployed to Iraq twice, with 3rd Battalion, 4th Marines and then 3rd Battalion, 7th Marines, and fought in the Battle of Husaybah.
After the Marines, built a career as a senior systems and network administrator in information technology.
Used the GI Bill to study applied math and physics at the University of Utah but ran out of funding before finishing, according to his survey.
Says he is a VA patient and a cancer survivor treated by the VA; lives in Salt Lake City.

priorities.text: Cites his grandmother's union pension and Social Security benefits as formative to his belief in social-insurance programs that support working families.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content was found; biography draws on his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Taylor Wright
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the April 18, 2026 Libertarian Party convention

summary.text: Taylor Wright is the Libertarian Party nominee for Utah's 4th Congressional District. He is an elementary school physical education teacher and longtime football coach who has also worked with adults with special needs.

background.text: Works as a physical education teacher at Ridge View Elementary School in Herriman, Utah.
Has coached football at the middle school, high school and college levels.
Has worked with adults with special needs and hosted a podcast called "Saving Humanity."

candidates.researchNotes: No birthplace, education, campaign website content or Candidate Connection survey found beyond the biographical facts above.

candidates.name: Steven Burt

summary.text: Steven Burt is an unaffiliated candidate for Utah's 4th Congressional District. An attorney who grew up in the district, he is running on loyalty to constituents rather than a party, term and age limits for members of Congress, a ban on congressional stock trading and housing affordability.

background.text: Graduated from Copper Hills High School; says he grew up in District 4, still lives there and has family and friends in the district.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University in 2003 and a law degree from the University of Utah in 2007.
Career experience includes working as an attorney.
Says he spent more than a year before the campaign listening to voters in the district.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content was found; biography draws on his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. Ballotpedia does not list his employers or earlier campaigns.
